title: Leverage Points
hook: One pricing change can do more than six months of grinding. It just feels too easy to count.
statement: Small moves in the right spot create massive change.
explainer: Some changes ripple into everything downstream. Price, offer, positioning. Others touch nothing. Working hard in a low-leverage spot feels productive but barely moves the business.
sop: List your levers: pricing, offer, positioning, a key hire, a process.
Score each one's Change and Leverage Multiplier 1 to 10.
Pick the top one and ignore the rest for 2 weeks.
Make the change and watch several metrics, not just one.
Only move to the next lever once this one is done.
equation_example: Change is 4, a single pricing tweak. Leverage Multiplier is 8, since it hits revenue, margin, and positioning. 4 × 8 = 32. Higher means a small change gets outsized results. A multiplier of 1 or 2 means hard work in the wrong spot.
question: Name the one lever you've been ignoring because it seems too simple.
closing_statement: The right small lever moves the most.
caption:
Principle Nº 109: Leverage Points
